intended_object: The R-algebra isomorphism A ≃ₐ[R] B coming from an isomorphism A ≅ B in the category of commutative R-algebras, i.e. one direction of the correspondence between categorical isomorphisms and algebra equivalences. Inferred from the docstring and from its use as `toFun` of the equivalence `(A ≅ B) ≃ (A ≃ₐ[R] B)` defined just below it in the file.
explanation: The definition takes the multiplicative, additive and `commutes` structure from the underlying algebra hom `i.hom.hom`. Its forward map is `i.hom` and its inverse is `i.inv`. The two inverse laws follow from `i.hom ≫ i.inv = 𝟙` and `i.inv ≫ i.hom = 𝟙`, which `simp` proves. So this is exactly the algebra equivalence induced by a categorical isomorphism. The file pairs it with `isoMk`, which goes the other way, to form an equivalence between isomorphisms in `CommAlgCat R` and algebra equivalences. A comparable conversion exists for `AlgCat` (`Iso.toAlgEquiv`), but it is for a different category, so there is no Mathlib duplicate of this definition. Requiring `R` to be a commutative ring is the setting in which `CommAlgCat` is defined, so the definition is not too narrow.
